atom_id: G11 Ev evolvability (R3/R4: kernel evolvability, metric sensitivity of Ev)
donor_source_ids: Price 1970 (Price equation; selection/transmission decomposition); selection-mutation balance (standard population-genetics form)
donor_structure: Price identity: change in mean trait = Cov(w_i, z_i)/w-bar + E(w_i * delta z_i)/w-bar - an exact bookkeeping decomposition into a selection term (covariance of fitness with trait) and a transmission term (fidelity of inheritance); the second term is where mutation/recombination noise enters; identity is exact, interpretation is where the theory lives.
target_structure: Ev = P(useful descendant | state, kernel): kernel evolvability. R3 needs Ev well-defined for kernels; R4 asks its metric sensitivity - how much Ev moves when the state/kernel moves (ladder already holds |Ev_Sigma - Ev_Sigma'| <= TV(Q_Sigma, Q_Sigma') as lane-F PARENT_SUFFICIENT via Dobrushin coupling).
mapping: fitness w -> usefulness indicator of descendant; trait z -> any state functional; selection covariance -> proposal-selection alignment (kernel mass on useful variants); transmission term -> kernel fidelity (noise/mutation in realizing the selected variant); delta z -> burden delta of the realized descendant.
preserved_relations: exact decomposition: expected change in Ev-relevant mass = alignment term + fidelity term, an identity-level transfer (no assumptions needed)
the transmission term is the honest location of kernel noise - matches the Dobrushin-coupling sensitivity bound: TV distance IS the transmission-fidelity budget
selection-mutation balance: steady-state useful-variant mass balances selection pull against mutation push - the equilibrium reading of Ev
known_broken_relations: Price equation is bookkeeping, not dynamics: it does not predict trajectories without a model of w and the transmission map (known criticism class in the donor literature itself)
biological fitness is exogenous; HSG usefulness is governed/verifier-dependent (G07) - the selection term is constitution-mediated, breaking direct interpretive transfer
Price covariance requires a population at each t; a single HSG lineage is a sample of size 1 - the identity applies to the ensemble/measure view only (R2/R3 measures, not individual orbits)
unknown_correspondences: whether the fidelity term admits a Dobrushin-style contraction bound across composed kernels (R5 interface) - natural next question, unowned
evolvability of the kernel-modifying process itself (G11's R6 row, lane G) has no Price-analogue parent
assumptions_added: usefulness event measurable (lane-E analytic+universal completion condition)
ensemble view: Ev evaluated on the state measure, not a single trajectory
candidate_theorem: Kernel evolvability decomposes exactly as Ev-change = selection-alignment covariance + transmission-fidelity term; the metric sensitivity of Ev is bounded by the transmission term's TV mass (consolidating the Dobrushin bound as the fidelity budget).
strongest_parent: Price 1970 (identity; standard) + Dobrushin coupling (already verified in ladder for G11 R4)
route: L0 x2 + L2 of Price-equation structure + map/synth/validate; validation: identity parent-owned and exact; the fidelity-budget consolidation with the existing Dobrushin bound is the residual contribution - checked for consistency, no counterexample
